newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to spend $8 bln on infrastructure to 2006.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to spend $8 bln on infrastructure to 2006.

text.p: Croatia plans to spend $8 billion in the next decade to rebuild infrastructure, including 1,300 km of highways, Reconstruction and Development Minister Jure Radic said on Friday.
He told an investment conference the government would look for foreign investors for its ambitious infrastructure package, worth $18 billion over a longer term.

"The government has prepared the plan and sent it to parliament," Radic said, adding it looked into all forms of joint projects with foreign partners, including concessions, loans and other forms of investments.
This year, only 47.5 km of highways are to be completed but plans for the future are to build 120-150 km of modern highways a year.
Among other big projects is a radical reconstruction of the railway system, parts of which Radic said were on a 19th century level. A line between capital Zagreb and Rijeka is the first on the list.
He also mentioned among priorities the modernisation of the Rijeka port which he said was poised to become the central port not only for Croatia but Central and Eastern Europe.
The plans include building of a 60 km channel between the rivers Sava and Danube which would shorten river communications between Zagreb and Budapest by 450 km.
Also, Radic said the government planned to launch an ecological project on the Adriatic by building a new sewage system, which has begun in and around Split.
"Croatian government is open and is hoping for the participation of foreign capital in these big infrastructure projects," he said.
